text: Ten fictional nonprofit programme passages, each with eight quote variants for citation-checker testing.

passages.source_passage: Welcome to the Lanternhouse Evening Literacy Network. As a volunteer tutor, you will usually work with groups of six to eight learners, meeting twice a week from 6:30 to 8:00 pm. In 2023, 41% of our learners were reading at a basic level after twelve weeks. Tutors should invite learners to choose the reading topic for each session. Do not correct every mistake aloud; learners who feel embarrassed often stop attending. Instead, note recurring errors and revisit them in the next session. Each centre keeps a box of graded readers, and tutors should never take these home without signing the loan sheet. If a learner misses three sessions in a row, contact your centre coordinator so that someone can follow up by phone within the week.

passages.source_passage: Board members will recall that the Sahelwood Schools Meal Initiative expanded to 38 primary schools in the Koubanda region in January 2024. Over the first term, kitchens served an average of 9,400 hot lunches per school day. Attendance rose from 71% to 83% in participating schools, although we cannot yet attribute the whole increase to meals. Parent committees now supervise cooks at every site, and local farmers supply roughly one third of the millet and beans. Deliveries were not always on time: during the rainy season, four schools went without rice for up to nine days. Management does not recommend further expansion until a second warehouse is secured in Dabori.

passages.source_passage: In 2024, the Mvuli District Health Partnership trained and deployed 212 community health workers across eleven sub-counties of Rangwe District. Each worker visited an average of 45 households per month, screening children for malnutrition and referring pregnant women to the nearest clinic. Facility deliveries in the district increased by 18% compared with the 2022 baseline. Supervisors coached health workers during monthly review meetings, which also served as a channel for restocking medicines. However, stock-outs of zinc and oral rehydration salts were not resolved, and nearly a quarter of workers reported at least one month without supplies. Stipends were never paid late during the year, which we believe contributed to the low dropout rate of 6%.

passages.source_passage: This mid-term evaluation of the Fairway Paralegal Outreach Service covers the period from March 2022 to August 2023. During that time, 17 paralegals held 640 mobile clinics in market towns of the Orvane Valley. Most cases concerned land disputes, inheritance and unpaid wages. Clients rated the service highly, with 88% saying they would recommend it to a neighbour. The evaluators did not find evidence that referrals to formal courts were tracked consistently, and few files recorded the final outcome. Paralegals supported village elders in mediating family disputes, a role the original design had not anticipated. We recommend that the second phase add a simple case-tracking tool and a refresher course of three days for all staff.

passages.source_passage: Between 4 and 22 July, the Clearwater Malaria Coalition distributed 56,300 long-lasting insecticidal nets in Teso Plains and Ubami districts. Distribution teams registered households in advance, allocating one net for every two people. Post-distribution checks in 300 randomly selected homes found that 79% of nets had been hung correctly. In Ubami, nets were not reaching some island villages because boats were unavailable during the fishing season. Monitors also observed that a few households used nets to cover seedlings, which is not the intended use. Community mobilisers will revisit these villages in October with demonstrations on hanging and washing nets. No serious safety incidents were reported during the campaign.

passages.source_passage: Update for the Board, November 2024. The Harvest Circle Savings Programme now supports 146 village savings and loan groups in Kelemba province, with 3,870 active members, of whom 72% are women. Total group savings reached the equivalent of 210,000 dollars this cycle. Groups lend to members at interest rates set by the members themselves, and the programme does not provide external capital. Repayment remained strong, but six groups in the flood-affected north did not complete their share-out on schedule. Field officers mentored group treasurers in record-keeping during the year. We are not proposing new groups in the north until roads reopen next spring.

passages.source_passage: During 2023, the Brightshore Coastal Readiness Project extended its early-warning network to 27 fishing villages along the Merrow coastline. Volunteers installed solar-powered sirens at 19 sites and trained 540 residents in evacuation procedures. When Cyclone Talia approached in May, alerts reached village committees about 30 hours before landfall. Nobody in the covered villages lost their life, although two shelters were overcrowded and lacked clean water. Several older residents did not evacuate because they feared their homes would be looted. Committees warned fishers about rising seas by radio, and the coast guard confirmed that no boats were caught at sea. In 2024 we plan to add three new shelters and review the needs of people with disabilities.

passages.source_passage: In the 2023–24 season, the Greenfurrow Farmer Field School Network ran 64 schools across the hill districts of Asante Ridge and Lomo. Each school brought together around 25 farmers on a demonstration plot for weekly sessions over sixteen weeks. Participants who adopted intercropping and mulching reported maize yields 35% higher than on their control plots. Extension officers trained lead farmers, who in turn facilitated sessions in their own villages. Uptake of composting was lower than expected, and many farmers did not have enough livestock manure. The drought in February wasn't severe enough to destroy crops, but it delayed planting by about three weeks. We have not yet measured changes in household income, which will be assessed in 2025.

passages.source_passage: The Little Acorn Playgroup Network completed its second full year in 2024, operating 52 community playgroups in the townships of Kessel Bay. Around 1,300 children aged three to five attended at least two mornings a week. Trained caregivers led play-based activities, while parents volunteered on a rota to prepare snacks and tidy materials. Developmental screening showed that 64% of children met age-appropriate milestones in language, up from 49% at entry. Playgroups did not charge fees, and no child was turned away for lack of a birth certificate. Retention of caregivers was a challenge: nine of the original caregivers left for paid preschool posts. Mothers mentored new caregivers informally in several sites, an arrangement we hope to formalise next year.

passages.source_passage: In the highland municipalities of San Tolomeo, fewer than four in ten girls who finish primary school go on to enrol in secondary education. Since 2019, the Camino Abierto Scholarship Fund has supported 380 girls with tuition, uniforms and transport stipends. Of those who began in the first cohort, 81% have graduated or remain enrolled. Distance remains the main barrier, and many communities have no secondary school within ten kilometres. Families have not been asked to contribute financially, which we consider essential for reaching the poorest households. Mentors meet scholars monthly to review attendance and grades. This proposal seeks support to add 150 new scholars over three years and to pilot a boarding allowance.
